name: Cape Town
tagline: Mountain, ocean and vineyards at the tip of Africa
description:
Few cities have a setting as outrageous as Cape Town's. A flat-topped mountain rises straight out of the city centre, the coastline unfurls in white-sand coves and granite boulders, and world-class vineyards roll out less than an hour away. Mornings start with a hike up Lion's Head, afternoons drift by on Camps Bay's promenade, and evenings end with a glass of Chenin Blanc as the sun sinks into the Atlantic.

It's also a city of complex, layered stories. The candy-coloured houses of the Bo-Kaap speak of Cape Malay heritage, Robben Island confronts the brutality of apartheid head-on, and the townships offer a vibrant, sobering contrast to the glossy V&A Waterfront. The food scene weaves every strand together, from fragrant Cape Malay curries to tasting menus that rank among Africa's finest.

Rent a car to drive the Cape Peninsula to Boulders Beach's penguins and the wild Cape of Good Hope, watch the wind forecast before heading up Table Mountain, and give yourself at least five days — almost everyone wishes they'd stayed longer.

safety.notes: Stick to busy, well-lit areas after dark and use Uber or Bolt instead of walking at night; hike popular trails in groups, as opportunistic muggings occur on some mountain routes. Never leave valuables visible in a parked car.

tipping: Tip 10–15% in restaurants, around R10–20 to the car guards who watch your parked car, and a similar amount to petrol-station attendants.
gettingAround: Uber and Bolt are cheap and the safest way around after dark; MyCiTi buses serve the centre, the Atlantic seaboard and the airport, while a rental car (driving on the left) is best for the peninsula and winelands.
tips: The Table Mountain cableway closes in high wind or thick cloud, so check its live status each morning and go up on the first clear day you get.
Book Robben Island ferry tickets several weeks ahead in summer — sailings sell out and are often cancelled in rough seas.
Atlantic beaches like Camps Bay and Clifton are breathtaking but icy (often 12–15°C); for warmer swims, head to False Bay beaches like Muizenberg or Boulders.
Drive the peninsula loop via Chapman's Peak in the morning and return along False Bay, stopping in Kalk Bay for fish and chips.
Pack a windbreaker even in summer — the south-easterly 'Cape Doctor' can blow for days and chill the warmest afternoon.
On the first Thursday of each month, city-centre galleries stay open late for a free art walk that spills onto the streets.
etiquette: Open any interaction with a greeting and a 'how are you?' — launching straight into a request comes across as rude.
'Just now' can mean anything from five minutes to a few hours, while 'now now' means soon; go with the flow.
Visit townships only with community-based local guides, and ask before photographing people or homes.
If you're invited to a braai (barbecue), bring your own drinks and some meat to share — it's the local custom.

neighborhoods.name: City Bowl
neighborhoods.blurb: The central amphitheatre beneath Table Mountain, taking in the CBD, leafy Gardens and Tamboerskloof, with Bree Street's restaurants and bars at its heart.

neighborhoods.name: Bo-Kaap
neighborhoods.blurb: Cobbled streets of brightly painted houses on the slopes of Signal Hill, the historic home of the Cape Malay community, with mosques, spice shops and home-style kitchens.

neighborhoods.name: Woodstock
neighborhoods.blurb: A gritty-cool former industrial suburb now filled with murals, design studios, galleries and weekend food markets.

neighborhoods.name: Sea Point
neighborhoods.blurb: An Atlantic-facing suburb with a long, lively promenade for jogging and sunsets, an ocean-fed public pool and diverse, good-value restaurants.

neighborhoods.name: Kalk Bay
neighborhoods.blurb: A charming False Bay fishing village of antique shops, bohemian cafés and a working harbour where you can buy fish straight off the boats.

dishes.name: Bobotie
dishes.description: Spiced minced meat baked with dried fruit under a golden egg custard — a Cape Malay classic served with yellow rice and chutney.

dishes.name: Gatsby
dishes.description: A foot-long roll crammed with slap chips, masala steak or polony and lashings of sauce, built to share and born on the Cape Flats.

dishes.name: Braaied snoek
dishes.description: A bony, full-flavoured local fish grilled over coals with a sticky apricot-jam glaze, eaten with sweet potatoes and fresh bread.

dishes.name: Koesister
dishes.description: The Cape Malay koesister: a spiced, doughnut-like dumpling dipped in syrup and rolled in coconut, traditionally eaten on Sunday mornings.

dishes.name: Malva pudding
dishes.description: A sticky, spongy apricot-jam pudding soaked in a warm cream sauce, usually served with custard or ice cream.

events.name: Cape Town Street Parade (Kaapse Klopse)
events.description: Around 2 January, minstrel troupes in sequined satin suits and parasols parade through the city with banjos and brass, a vibrant tradition known as Tweede Nuwe Jaar.

events.name: Cape Town Cycle Tour
events.description: One of the world's largest timed cycle races sends tens of thousands of riders around the peninsula via Chapman's Peak, turning the city into a festival.

events.name: Cape Town Carnival
events.description: A glittering night-time street parade of giant floats, dancers and musicians along the Green Point Fan Walk, celebrating the city's diversity.

events.name: Two Oceans Marathon
events.description: Over the Easter weekend, runners tackle an ultra and half marathon along some of the most beautiful race routes on the planet.

attractions.name: Table Mountain
attractions.description: The city's flat-topped backdrop rises more than a kilometre above the sea, reached by a rotating cable car or a steep two-to-three-hour hike up Platteklip Gorge. Up top, easy paths wind through fynbos, one of the richest plant kingdoms on Earth, to viewpoints over the Twelve Apostles, Robben Island and the Atlantic seaboard.
attractions.hours: Cableway roughly 08:00–19:30 in summer, 08:30–18:00 in winter, weather permitting
attractions.bookingTip: Buy an online ticket for an early car and check the cableway's live status — it shuts without warning when the wind picks up or the 'tablecloth' cloud rolls in.

attractions.name: Robben Island
attractions.description: Nelson Mandela spent 18 of his 27 prison years on this windswept island, and the ferry crossing, bus tour and walk through the maximum-security prison — including his tiny cell — are deeply moving. Former political prisoners have long guided visitors, adding first-hand testimony.
attractions.hours: Ferries typically at 09:00, 11:00, 13:00 and 15:00 from the V&A Waterfront, weather permitting
attractions.bookingTip: Book online weeks ahead and check for cancellations that morning — rough seas often halt sailings.

attractions.name: V&A Waterfront
attractions.description: A working harbour turned sprawling leisure district of shops, restaurants, markets and an aquarium, framed by Table Mountain and lounging Cape fur seals. The craft and food markets are great places to sample local design and cooking under one roof.
attractions.bookingTip: It's one of the city's safest areas after dark, making it ideal for a sunset drink before dinner.

attractions.name: Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden
attractions.description: Draped over the eastern slopes of Table Mountain, this celebrated garden showcases South Africa's extraordinary flora, from king proteas to ancient cycads. Walk the curving 'Boomslang' canopy walkway through the treetops, and come back on summer Sundays for sunset concerts on the lawns.
attractions.bookingTip: Summer sunset-concert tickets sell out fast — book online as soon as the season's line-up is announced.

attractions.name: Bo-Kaap
attractions.description: Steep cobbled streets lined with houses painted lime, pink and turquoise climb Signal Hill in the city's historic Cape Malay quarter. Visit the small local museum, browse the spice shops and join a class in a family kitchen to learn the area's fragrant curries.
attractions.hours: Streets open 24 hours; museum roughly 09:00–16:00 Mon–Sat
attractions.bookingTip: This is a living residential community — be respectful when photographing homes and don't pose on people's doorsteps.

attractions.name: Cape of Good Hope
attractions.description: At the rugged tip of the Cape Peninsula, a reserve of windswept fynbos, ostriches and baboons ends in dramatic cliffs pounded by the Atlantic at the most south-westerly point of Africa. Ride the funicular up to the old lighthouse at Cape Point for dizzying ocean views.
attractions.bookingTip: Keep food out of sight and car windows closed — the baboons are bold and expert at raiding.

attractions.name: Boulders Beach
attractions.description: Giant granite boulders shelter a string of coves in Simon's Town where a colony of endangered African penguins waddles, nests and brays just metres away. Boardwalks give close-up views, and at the neighbouring cove you can swim in calm water alongside them.
attractions.bookingTip: Arrive at opening before the tour coaches, and never try to touch the penguins — their beaks are sharp.

attractions.name: Camps Bay
attractions.description: A palm-lined arc of white sand beneath the jagged Twelve Apostles, backed by a strip of buzzing cafés and cocktail bars. The water is bracingly cold, but the sunsets over the Atlantic are among the best in the city.
attractions.bookingTip: Parking is a nightmare on summer weekends — take an Uber or the MyCiTi bus from the city centre.

attractions.name: Zeitz MOCAA
attractions.wiki: Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa
attractions.description: Carved out of a 1920s grain silo, this museum's cathedral-like atrium — sliced through the old concrete tubes — is a jaw-dropping piece of architecture in its own right. Its galleries showcase contemporary art from across Africa and its diaspora.
attractions.bookingTip: Book online to skip the ticket queue, then pair your visit with lunch in the surrounding Silo District.

attractions.name: Lion's Head
attractions.description: A spiralling trail climbs this distinctive granite peak to a 360-degree summit view over Table Mountain, the City Bowl and the Atlantic coastline. The final stretch uses chains and ladders — or a gentler bypass — and full-moon hikes are a much-loved local ritual.
attractions.hours: Open 24 hours; hike in daylight or with a group
attractions.bookingTip: Start early to beat the heat and the parking chaos at the trailhead, and carry a headlamp if you go up for sunset.

hotels.name: Kaapse Kroon Hotel
hotels.description: A glass-and-stone tower at the water's edge where every suite frames Table Mountain across the marina. The spa's saltwater pool faces the harbour, and the concierge can arrange helicopter flips along the Atlantic coast.

hotels.name: Kleurhuis Bo-Kaap
hotels.description: A cluster of restored 19th-century cottages painted in the neighbourhood's signature colours, with rooftop views over the city to the harbour. Breakfast features koesisters and spiced eggs from the owner's family recipes.

hotels.name: Dassiekop Backpackers
hotels.description: A friendly hostel in a rambling Victorian house on the lower slopes of Table Mountain, with a pool, braai area and bar where travellers swap trail tips. Staff lead group hikes up Platteklip Gorge and Lion's Head several times a week.

hotels.name: Kelpwoud Design Hotel
hotels.description: Board-marked concrete, kelp-green tiles and driftwood furniture give this Sea Point hotel a coastal-brutalist edge, with ocean-facing balconies and a rooftop plunge pool gazing up at Lion's Head. The promenade is right across the road.

hotels.name: Kasteelsig Beach Apartments
hotels.description: Airy self-catering apartments above Camps Bay with full kitchens, braai-equipped balconies and sweeping views of the Twelve Apostles. The beach and café strip are a three-minute walk downhill.

hotels.name: Rietdak Homestead
hotels.description: A thatched Cape Dutch farmhouse from the 1800s set in oak-shaded gardens near Kirstenbosch, with whitewashed gables, yellowwood floors and a pool in the old orchard. The Constantia wine route begins just down the road.

restaurants.name: Salie's Gatsby Hatch
restaurants.description: A hole-in-the-wall hatch on the edge of the Bo-Kaap, where Salie builds foot-long Gatsbys loaded with masala steak, slap chips and peri-peri sauce. A whole one easily feeds three, so order a quarter unless you're ravenous.

restaurants.name: Tafelkleed Café
restaurants.description: A sunny café at the foot of the mountain where hikers refuel with shakshuka, rooibos lattes and just-baked buttermilk rusks before hitting the trails. Grab a picnic pack to enjoy at the top.
restaurants.signatureDish: Buttermilk rusks with a rooibos latte

restaurants.name: Renosterveld
restaurants.description: A 12-course menu that roams the Cape's landscapes — Karoo lamb, West Coast mussels, foraged veld herbs — plated like artworks in a room overlooking the harbour. The wine pairing is a masterclass in Chenin Blanc and Syrah from small producers.
restaurants.signatureDish: Karoo lamb with smoked buchu jus

restaurants.name: Kaneel & Borrie
restaurants.description: A family kitchen serving fragrant Cape Malay dishes from generations-old recipes: bobotie, chicken curry with flaky roti and sweet-sour denningvleis. Finish with a syrupy, coconut-dusted koesister.

restaurants.name: Snoekbraai Harbour Shack
restaurants.description: A tin-roofed shack by the harbour grilling snoek, calamari and yellowtail over coals, with hake and chips wrapped in paper for the road. Sit on the jetty and watch the fishing boats come in.

restaurants.name: Vuur & Klip
restaurants.description: An open kitchen with a roaring wood fire where dry-aged sirloin, boerewors and lamb chops are cooked braai-style and served with pap, chakalaka and grilled mielies. The wine list is a tour of Stellenbosch and the Swartland.

restaurants.name: Kaigan Izakaya
restaurants.description: Sea Point's favourite izakaya pairs pristine local tuna and yellowtail sashimi with charcoal-grilled yakitori and a thoughtful list of sake and Japanese whisky. Counter seats face the robata grill.

restaurants.name: Sonsak Terrace
restaurants.description: A breezy first-floor terrace facing the Atlantic, built for sundowners: West Coast oysters, grilled line fish and a long list of local Méthode Cap Classique sparkling wines. Book a railing table for sunset.
restaurants.signatureDish: West Coast oysters with Cap Classique

experiences.name: Cape Peninsula Loop: Penguins, Point and Chapman's Peak
experiences.description: Circle the whole peninsula in a small group, twisting along Chapman's Peak, meeting the penguins at Boulders, walking up to the Cape Point lighthouse and spotting ostriches and baboons in the reserve. Lunch is fish and chips in a harbour village.

experiences.name: Sunrise Lion's Head Scramble with a Mountain Guide
experiences.description: Start in the dark with a registered mountain guide, spiralling up to the summit in time to watch dawn light spill over Table Mountain and the Atlantic. Your guide handles route-finding on the chains and shares stories of the fynbos along the way.
includes: Coffee and rusks at the summit

experiences.name: Bo-Kaap Spice Walk and Cape Malay Cooking Class
experiences.description: Walk the cobbled streets with a Bo-Kaap resident to learn the area's history, then roll roti, fold samoosas and simmer a fragrant curry in her family kitchen. Lunch is everything you've made, with homemade ginger beer.

experiences.name: Atlantic Sunset Catamaran with Bubbly
experiences.description: Sail out of the harbour along the Atlantic seaboard towards the Clifton beaches as the sun drops into the ocean, often with seals and dolphins riding alongside. A glass of Cape sparkling wine is included.
